B MODELLING BODY MASS (20 marks)
You are advised to spend no more than 45 minutes on this part.
This task looks at three different models for the approximate body mass of an adult.
1 Here is a simple model to calculate the approximate body mass of an adult.
Measure the height in centimetres and subtract 100 to get the approximate mass in kilograms.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the approximate body mass of an adult who is 1.8 m tall.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the height of an adult who has an approximate body mass of 50 kg.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
For a height, h metres, the approximate body mass is M kilograms.
Find the formula for M in terms of h.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Sketch, showing appropriate scales, the graph of the approximate body mass, M.
th
2 In the 19 century, the Belgian mathematician Quetelet suggested a different model.
In his model the approximate body mass of an adult, Mkg, varies as the square of the height, h metres.
For an adult with height 2 m the approximate body mass is 88 kg.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that Quetelet’s model can be written as M = 22h .

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Show that an adult with height 1.5 m has an approximate body mass of 49.5 kg.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An adult has an approximate body mass of 77 kg.
Calculate the height of this adult.
3 (a) For some adults the simple model and Quetelet’s model give the same approximate body mass.
Find the height of these adults.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
For most adults, which model gives a larger approximate body mass?
Explain your answer.
4 Quetelet’s model gives an approximate body mass which is too small for taller people.
A modern model uses M = kh and the following information.
The approximate body mass of an adult is
78 kg for a height of 1.84 m
and 50 kg for a height of 1.54 m.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write down two equations in terms of k and n.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Show that n = 2.5, correct to one decimal place.

parts.label: (d)
